title: Shrimp in Garlic Sauce, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp in garlic sauce, Puerto Rican style is a dish of large peeled shrimp sautéed in a fragrant sauce made from garlic, olive oil, lime, cilantro and spices typical of Puerto Rican cuisine. The result is a bright, slightly spicy flavor with citrus and herb notes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puerto Rican cuisine blends Spanish, African and Indigenous influences, reflected in the use of garlic, lime and cilantro.
The garlic sauce is often based on olive oil and vinegar, making it lighter than creamy sauces.
Shrimp are one of the most popular seafoods in the Caribbean due to their fast growth and availability.
Traditionally the dish is served with rice, beans or fried plantains.
In Puerto Rico a “mojo” sauce—garlic and olive oil based—is commonly used as a base for this dish.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other seafood, shrimp contain very little saturated fat.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium supports immune function and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp are rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Small amounts of EPA and DHA contribute to heart and brain health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Foodborne toxins
items.content: Improperly stored shrimp can harbor bacteria and toxins that cause food poisoning.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: If the sauce includes soy sauce or added salt, the dish can become high in sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or appetizer. Shrimp in garlic sauce pairs well with rice, quinoa, fried plantains or a fresh salad. Squeeze additional lime juice before serving to brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag and use within a month. Reheat thoroughly until the shrimp are hot throughout.
